standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Properties of Spaces, label spaces-properties-lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover (invoked at proof lines 1406 and 1419)

standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Decent Spaces, label decent-spaces-lemma-bounded-fibres (invoked at proof lines 1409 and 1422)
standard_prerequisites.use: It produces the integer $d$ bounding the degrees of the fibres of $U \to X$ and the integers $d_p$ bounding the degrees of $V_p \to U_p$.

standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-compactness and separatedness of the quotients of the configuration schemes
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Spaces, label spaces-lemma-quotient-finite-separated (invoked at proof line 1416)
standard_prerequisites.use: Since $X$ is quasi-separated the schemes $W_p$ are quasi-compact and separated, hence the quotients $U_p = W_p/S_{p+1}$ are too.

standard_prerequisites.name: The alternating Cech spectral sequence, the vanishing on the separated case, and quasi-coherence of the twists
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, labels lemma-alternating-spectral-sequence (invoked at proof line 1434), proposition-vanishing (invoked at proof line 1436) and lemma-quasi-coherent-twist (invoked at proof line 1438)
standard_prerequisites.use: The spectral sequence computes the cohomology of $X$ from the twisted cohomology of the $U_p$; the second ingredient makes those groups vanish above $d_p$; the third keeps the twisted sheaves quasi-coherent so that the vanishing applies.

core_obligations: Choose the data: an affine $U$ with a surjective etale morphism to $X$, the integer $d$ bounding the fibre degrees, and for each $p$ an affine $V_p$ mapping surjectively and etale onto the quotient $U_p$ with degree bound $d_p$ (proof lines 1404-1423).

Show that the quotients $U_p = W_p/S_{p+1}$ are quasi-compact and separated: the configuration schemes $W_p$ are quasi-compact because $X$ is quasi-separated and separated because $U$ is separated (proof lines 1411-1416).

Use the alternating Cech spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q} = H^q(U_p, \mathcal{F}|_{U_p} \otimes_{\mathbf{Z}} \underline{\mathbf{Z}}(\chi_p)) \Rightarrow H^{p+q}(X, \mathcal{F})$, and note $U_p = 0$ for $p \geq d$ (proof lines 1425-1435).

Apply the separated vanishing result and the quasi-coherence of the twists to see that the $E_1$-terms vanish for $q \geq d_p$, and conclude $H^q(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for $q \geq \max(d_p + p)$ (proof lines 1436-1443).
proof_roadmap: Construction of the covers and the degree bounds (proof lines 1404-1423).
Quasi-compactness and separatedness of the configuration quotients (proof lines 1411-1416).
The spectral sequence and the range of $p$ (proof lines 1425-1435).
Vanishing of the $E_1$-terms and the conclusion (proof lines 1436-1443).
difficulty_reason: The lemma provides, for a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space, a system of affine covers and degree bounds whose maximum controls the cohomological dimension for quasi-coherent sheaves (statement lines 1384-1401). The proof builds the data using boundedness of fibres and the configuration quotients, checks that those quotients are quasi-compact and separated, feeds them into the alternating Cech spectral sequence, and kills the $E_1$-terms in the required range by the separated vanishing result combined with quasi-coherence of the twists. The bookkeeping of the spectral sequence range is the substance, so the claim is H2.
